failure_conditions.condition: A factual claim, citation, technical statement, calculation, interpretation, source representation, or comparable epistemic artefact is generated, retrieved, transformed, inferred, or synthesised.
failure_conditions.assessment: Displayed health summaries are factual synthesis artefacts.

failure_conditions.condition: The output has an evidenced intended purpose or downstream task for which factual accuracy, evidentiary fidelity, technical correctness, source integrity, traceability, uncertainty handling or equivalent epistemic assurance is materially consequential; identify the requirement for the actual workflow stage, including any drafting function.
failure_conditions.assessment: Health-search answers invite materially consequential understanding and care decisions.

failure_conditions.condition: The content accuracy, specificity, certainty, framing or assurance applied to the artefact is materially below the level required for that purpose and reliance condition.
failure_conditions.assessment: Reported examples omit clinically essential context; specialist challenges concern substantive fitness, not mere citation source prestige.

failure_conditions.condition: The artefact is supplied, represented, propagated, incorporated, submitted or accepted as usable for the reliance-bearing purpose or workflow stage without its required accuracy or epistemic threshold being satisfied. Draft status or an expectation of later human review does not by itself establish fitness for that purpose.
failure_conditions.assessment: Answers were displayed directly; later show-more warnings do not guarantee initial advice remains provisionally bounded.

failure_conditions.condition: The mismatch materially affects or creates a material risk to decision-making, evidentiary use, professional work, institutional process, public reliance, technical correctness, or another reliance-bearing outcome.
failure_conditions.assessment: Potential care distortion suffices without a proven injured patient.

success_conditions.condition: An epistemic artefact is proposed for reliance with material error consequences.

Content accuracy and assurance meet the requirement for the actual purpose and workflow stage. Specificity, certainty and framing remain proportionate to source quality, independence, traceability, uncertainty and temporal fitness, without distorting material meaning.
success_conditions.assessment: Challenged content was not shown fit for the actual clinical use.

success_conditions.condition: The output, supporting evidence and reliance decision demonstrate fitness for that bounded use and show that lower-assurance material remained restricted from unsupported higher reliance. A provisional label or an expectation of human review alone is insufficient.
success_conditions.assessment: Removal of two exact queries does not show protective coverage across variants.

exclusion_comparison: Not fiction or tolerated approximation when omitted context materially changes advice. Professional-help disclaimer does not cure unsuitable content for the supplied task. No required-check-only, stale verification or provenance-only explanation.
amendment_delta: Explicit operational reliance applies to the trace-linked decisions above; no bad-outcome-to-belief inference. Hindsight-only mistake does not prove insufficient assurance; known boundary crossing without separate assurance defect excluded. Success requires responsive bounded use, not mere recognition.

before_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Inaccurate and context-deficient medical synthesis appeared as a direct answer to high-stakes health queries at an assurance level unsuitable for consequential reliance. A material medical caution was produced but routed only into an expanded low-salience view after the initial answer, so it did not reach the reader at the first reliance point. The interface included a medical caution in an expandable low-salience section. A produced warning therefore reached a capable reading surface, contrary to the prior all-endpoints non-delivery assumption. It remains unknown whether this qualified as an operative protective control whose timing and effect met the applicable purpose. The established first-display visibility defect is distinct from the unresolved protective-effect assessment.

Specialist groups criticised the missing clinical context. The reporting demonstrates the displayed answers, not that any identifiable patient acted on them or sustained injury.
